text: Caterpillar's Q1 2026 release named changes in dealer inventories before higher sales of equipment to end users as the drivers of higher CI sales volume.
The Q1 2026 release said higher sales volume was mainly driven by the impact from changes in dealer inventories and higher sales of equipment to end users.
quote: Higher sales volume was mainly driven by the impact from changes in dealer inventories and higher sales of equipment to end users.

text: Caterpillar's Q2 2026 release named higher sales of equipment to end users before changes in dealer inventories as the drivers of higher CI sales volume.
The Q2 2026 release said higher sales volume was mainly driven by higher sales of equipment to end users and by the impact from changes in dealer inventories.
quote: Higher sales volume was mainly driven by higher sales of equipment to end users and by the impact from changes in dealer inventories.

text: Management's primary stated volume driver shifted from dealer inventories (Q1 2026) to end users (Q2 2026).
Caterpillar's CFO put the Q2 2026 tariff impact on Construction Industries margin at 340 bps.
The CFO said Construction Industries margin was impacted by 340 basis points of tariffs in Q2 2026.
Management placed most of the $392M IEEPA tariff recoveries in corporate items.
The CFO said the majority of the IEEPA recoveries was reflected in corporate items.
quote: with the majority of this amount reflected in corporate items.

text: CI segment margin is not materially inflated by the IEEPA recoveries.
The Q1 2026 CI dealer-inventory build was $1.5 billion, against a decrease in the prior-year quarter.
The CFO called the Q1 2026 build a more typical first-quarter increase, compared with a slight decrease in the prior year.
quote: a more typical $1.5 billion increase in the first quarter as compared to a slight decrease in the prior year.

text: CI dealer inventory increased by $400 million in Q2 2026.
Management said dealer inventory increased by 400 million dollars in Construction Industries compared to a decrease in the second quarter of 2025.
quote: Dealer inventory increased by 400 million dollars in Construction Industries compared to a decrease in the second quarter of 2025.

text: The releases said unfavorable CI manufacturing costs in Q4 2025 and Q1 2026 largely reflected higher tariff costs.
The Q2 2026 CI segment profit increase was primarily due to higher sales volume.
The Q2 2026 release said the increase was primarily due to the profit impact of higher sales volume.
quote: The increase was primarily due to the profit impact of higher sales volume

text: CI North America dealer inventory decreased in Q2 2025, after remaining about flat in Q2 2024.
The release said North America dealer inventory decreased during the second quarter of 2025.
quote: Dealer inventory decreased during the second quarter of 2025, while remaining about flat during the second quarter of 2024.

text: CI Asia/Pacific dealer inventory increased in Q3 2025, against a decrease a year earlier.
The release said Asia/Pacific dealer inventory increased during the third quarter of 2025.
quote: Dealer inventory increased during the third quarter of 2025, compared with a decrease during the third quarter of 2024.

text: Management expects a dealer-inventory drawdown in Q4 2026.

Management guided full-year 2026 tariff cost, excluding the expected IEEPA tariff recoveries of approximately 400 million dollars reported in the second quarter, to about $2.2 billion, with roughly half of Q3 2026 tariff costs in CI.
CI growth was still heavily supported by dealer restocking in Q1 2026, but by Q2 2026 the mix had shifted materially toward end-user demand.
Cash flow does not independently confirm the stocking thesis: Q1 2026 operating cash flow was stronger than Q1 2025.
Ex-tariff CI margin is an upper bound on underlying performance, because price realization was taken partly to recover the same tariff costs.
